subject: Pilot top-up or short extension — ClearForge evaluation
messages:
From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@clearforge.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — 2-week extension or top-up for pilot

Hi David,

Quick note from our side — we ran into some delays in integrating ClearForge's ingestion pipeline and didn't get the final workload profile we expected into the pilot. We have about 7 business days left on the current time-boxed evaluation but ~30% of the workload scenarios are still outstanding.

Can Redwood do either:
- a 14-day courtesy extension to the pilot so we can finish the integration and run the last set of tests, or
- a one-time top-up of additional inference credits at a discounted rate if we can't extend the timeline?

If possible, we'd prefer the extension but would accept a top-up if there's a meaningful discount (something in the range of 15–25%). We're aiming to make an internal recommendation by next Friday.

I attached a short metrics snapshot (see ClearForge_Metrics.xlsx) so you can see where we are.

Thanks — appreciate any flexibility.

Best,
Alex
Alex Ruiz
Head of Product
ClearForge
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@clearforge.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 2-week extension or top-up for pilot

Hi Alex — thanks for the context and the metrics. Sorry to hear about the ingestion delay — we've seen that pattern before and want to make it easy to complete the evaluation.

Two options from our side that I can put on the table quickly:

1) Short extension: 14 calendar days added to the current pilot at no additional cost. We can draft an amendment that keeps the same SLAs and support cadence.

2) Top-up: one-time credit pack equal to 20% of your original pilot allocation purchased at a 15% discount. This would be invoiced upfront but applied immediately so you can run the remaining tests.

If neither of these lands, we can explore a blended approach (e.g., 7 extra days + a smaller top-up).

Next steps: if you want the extension I can put a short amendment in DocuSign for signature; if you want the top-up I can generate an order and apply the discount. Which do you prefer?

Attachments: ClearForge_Metrics.xlsx (xlsx)

—
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Laura / Marissa — forwarding ClearForge's request. They missed some integration work and want either a 14-day extension or a discounted top-up. They prefer the extension but the customer will accept a 15–25% top-up discount.

My recommendation: approve either of the following and let me close it quickly on the thread:
- Option A (preferred): 14-day extension — no revenue impact, keeps momentum, we ask them to confirm new completion date and agree to a short success checklist.
- Option B (if finance/legal requires revenue): top-up equal to 20% of pilot allocation at up to 15% discount (we absorb a small discount but keep the purchase).

Please advise: I can offer up to 15% discount without escalations; anything higher would need manager OK.

—
David
